senate.title: U.S. Senate
senate.one: Votes on laws for the whole country. Georgia gets two senators, and one seat is up this year.
senate.why: They also approve or block the President's picks, including Supreme Court justices.
also: Georgia's other seat (Raphael Warnock) is up in 2028

house.title: U.S. House
house.one: Also votes on national laws, but speaks for your district instead of the whole state.
house.why: Your closest voice in Washington, and you get to keep or replace them every two years.

governor.title: Governor
governor.one: Runs the state and signs or vetoes every bill the legislature passes.
governor.why: Shapes how Georgia spends its money on schools, roads, and health care.
also: Can veto single items out of the budget
Commands the State Patrol and National Guard
Brian Kemp has hit the two-term limit, so this seat is wide open

ltgov.title: Lieutenant Governor
ltgov.one: Runs the State Senate's meetings and takes over if the governor can't serve.
ltgov.why: Has a hand in which bills move forward in the State Senate.

sos.title: Secretary of State
sos.why: Handles voter registration and certifies the results. Also licenses businesses and lots of professions.

ag.title: Attorney General
ag.one: Georgia's top lawyer. Represents the state in court.
ag.why: Goes after scams, shady debt collectors, misleading ads, and data breaches.
also: Can win refunds for people who got ripped off

agr.title: Agriculture Commissioner
agr.one: This job covers a lot more than farms.
agr.why: Inspects grocery stores for food safety, checks that gas pumps give you what you pay for, and tests store scales.
also: Bottled water, pet food, and fertilizer

ins.title: Insurance Commissioner
ins.one: Keeps insurance companies in check, and is also the state fire marshal.
ins.why: Reviews car, home, and health insurance rates, and takes your complaint if an insurer does you wrong.

labor.title: Labor Commissioner
labor.one: Runs the state Department of Labor.
labor.why: If you lose your job, this office handles your unemployment check. It also helps with job searches and training.

schools.title: School Superintendent
schools.one: Leads Georgia's public schools, kindergarten through 12th grade.
schools.why: Sends state money to local schools, pre-K, and the HOPE Scholarship.

psc3.title: Public Service Commission · District 3
psc3.one: Sets what Georgia Power can charge you for electricity.
psc3.why: Their decisions show up on your power bill. They also approve new power plants.
also: Doesn't cover water, cell phones, cable, or electric co-op rates
Every Georgian votes on every seat. Candidates just have to live in the district

psc5.title: Public Service Commission · District 5
psc5.one: A second seat on the commission that sets your power rates.
psc5.why: Same deal as District 3: everyone in Georgia votes on this one.

sen.title: State Senate
sen.one: Writes Georgia's laws and passes the state budget. There are 56 state senators.
sen.why: State laws cover schools, roads, voting rules, criminal law, and state taxes.

rep.title: State House
rep.one: The other half of the legislature. There are 180 state representatives, each with a smaller district than a senator's.
rep.why: Every bill has to pass here and in the State Senate before the governor can sign it.

amend.title: Amendment 1: Farm & Timber Land Tax Break
amend.one: Land used for farming or timber gets a property tax break, capped at 2,000 acres per owner. This would raise the cap to 4,000.
amend.why: YES raises the cap to 4,000 acres. NO keeps it at 2,000.
amend.ballot: Shall the Constitution of Georgia, for the purpose of protecting family farmland, be amended so as to increase the maximum acreage to qualify for assessment and taxation as a bona fide conservation use property from 2,000 acres to 4,000 acres?

source.label: Georgia Secretary of State, amendments booklet

amend2.title: Amendment 2: Nonpartisan Probate Judges
amend2.one: Probate judges handle wills, estates, guardianships, and marriage licenses. In many counties they already run without a party label, but in some they still run as a Democrat or Republican.
amend2.why: YES means every probate judge runs without a party label. NO keeps things as they are.
amend2.ballot: Shall the Constitution of Georgia be amended so as to require that all probate court judges be elected in nonpartisan elections?

source.label: Georgia Secretary of State, amendments booklet

amend3.title: Amendment 3: Fund for 911 Systems
amend3.one: Lets state lawmakers set aside some existing state money in a fund that can only be used to run, maintain, and expand 911 emergency call systems.
amend3.why: YES allows the separate 911 fund. NO keeps things as they are.
amend3.ballot: Shall the Constitution of Georgia be amended so as to authorize the General Assembly to dedicate certain existing revenues, including revenues reallocated by law, to a nonlapsing fund to be used exclusively for the expansion, maintenance, and operation of emergency 9-1-1 systems in this state?

source.label: Georgia Secretary of State, amendments booklet
